ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Skill, CardRarity.Rare, TargetType.Self)` (Stoke.cs:14-17) == cost 1 / SKILL / RARE / SELF. No keywords, no CanonicalVars -- the count is the hand size.

OnPlay.rationale: All four steps and their order match, and the RNG is handled CORRECTLY -- one of only four cards in the pool that gets this right. C#: snapshot the hand and its count (`List<CardModel> list = PileType.Hand.GetPile(Owner).Cards.ToList(); int exhaustCount = list.Count;`, Stoke.cs:22-23), exhaust every card in the snapshot one at a time (24-27), generate `exhaustCount` cards with `CardFactory.GetForCombat(characterPool, exhaustCount, Owner.RunState.Rng.CombatCardGeneration)` -- WITH replacement, so duplicates are allowed (28) -- upgrade them all if this card is upgraded (29-32), and add them to hand (33). The sim reproduces every step: `hand = list(ctx.player.hand)` then per-card `ExhaustCmd.exhaust`, then `get_for_combat_parity(crng.card_gen, len(hand))` under parity with the shared-rng `random_pool_cards(..., len(hand))` kept only for non-parity RL runs (stoke.py:111-115), then per-card upgrade and `add_to_hand`. Taking the count BEFORE the exhausts is load-bearing on both sides -- a Dark Embrace draw during the exhausts must not change how many cards are generated -- and both iterate a COPY so mutating the hand mid-loop is safe. Stoke itself is never in the snapshot (Play pile in C#, discard-pile limbo in the sim). Presentation, folded in: TriggerAnim (21) and `CardPreviewStyle.None` on the upgrade call (31).

OnUpgrade.rationale: Stoke.cs declares NO OnUpgrade override -- the upgrade changes no printed number, it upgrades the GENERATED cards, read from `IsUpgraded` inside OnPlay. The sim mirrors that exactly, including having no `_on_upgrade`. Same shape as card/armaments, card/cascade, card/primal_force and card/splash.
